grh_ac9663d85f7897a0364c.title: The Lady Gambles
paragraphs: Newspaper wife Joan Booth accompanies her husband David to Las Vegas and treats casino gambling as harmless vacation excitement. A small win and the attention of casino manager Corrigan awaken a compulsion she cannot control; soon she is borrowing money, chasing losses, lying to David, and choosing the tables over her marriage. Her addiction carries her from respectable casinos to private games and eventually to the bottom, where she is found beaten and nearly destroyed after a year away from her husband. David refuses to abandon her and works with doctors to uncover the fear, resentment, and family wounds feeding the obsession. A final emotional confrontation with her sister Ruth forces Joan to face the truth instead of escaping into gambling. When David reaches for her, Joan finally reaches back, accepts his help, and leaves with him determined to begin again.

grh_ace5a2edbd3b49e5513f.title: Her Husbands Affair
paragraphs: Margaret Weldon loves her ambitious husband Bill, but his confidence repeatedly outruns his judgment, especially when he throws himself into the inventions of an eccentric professor. A new cream is promoted as a hair remover, only to produce the opposite result and leave its test subjects sprouting alarming amounts of hair. With lawsuits and the governor furious, Margaret recognizes that the failed remover is actually a potentially valuable hair restorer and turns the disaster into a commercial opportunity. Bill resents her habit of rescuing his schemes and makes her promise to stop interfering, but almost immediately the professor arrives with another accidental invention, a fluid that preserves flowers indefinitely. Bill forgets every lesson he has just learned and eagerly launches the next venture with Margaret at his side.

grh_ac245eac81e54b47d0e2.title: A Leading Case
paragraphs: In 1890s San Francisco, Cordelia Botkin begins an affair with newspaperman John Dunning, whose wife and child are living with her family in Dover, Delaware. When Dunning decides to end the relationship and return to his wife, Cordelia becomes desperate. A package of poisoned candy sent east kills Dunning's wife and her sister, and investigators trace the arsenic purchase and other evidence back to Cordelia. Her trial then raises a novel jurisdiction question because the poison was mailed from California but the deaths occurred in Delaware. The California court rejects the defense challenge, Cordelia is convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life imprisonment, making the case a lasting legal precedent.

grh_ac418dd241608d277c3e.title: 3 Farthings for Your Thoughts
paragraphs: Harry joins Helen Barrett in a hunt for the £20,000 stolen by her imprisoned husband Bill. Bill has hidden the clue in three farthings and a letter referring to Beethoven; a maid and Bill's former partner Baxter are after the same money. After Bill is killed and Baxter corners Harry and Helen, Harry overpowers him and realizes the final clue points to Beethoven's 'Fury Over a Lost Farthing' among Bill's music records, where the money is hidden. The police arrive before Harry can profit, and his false pose as a bank-insurance investigator gets him deported instead.
